simple.meaning: גִּלָּיוֹן (gillâyôwn) is a Hebrew object word meaning “a tablet for writing (as bare ); by analogy, a mirror (as a plate ).” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Isaiah 3:23. The background is built from the passages where the word occurs.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to גִּלָּיוֹן (H1549) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: גִּלָּיוֹן (gillâyôwn) / H1549 is traced through Isaiah 3:23, Isaiah 8:1 with generated occurrence evidence.

definitions.short: a tablet for writing (as bare ); by analogy, a mirror (as a plate )
definitions.full: H1549. gillayon גִּלָּיוֺן noun masculine table, tablet (Talmud גִּלְיוֺן , the empty margin of page or roll, see Lag GN 1881, 403 , compare BN 199) — עָלָיו וּכְתֹב גָּדוֺל גִּלָּיוֺן קַחלְֿךָ take thee a great tablet and write upon it Isa 8:1 ; plural הַגִּלְֹינִים tablets of polished metal, mirrors 3:23 ᵑ9 ᵑ7 Ges Che Di De; but transparent garments, gauzes , ᵐ5 Ew (compare Arabic fine garment ).

occurrences.englishText: the hand mirrors, the fine linen garments, the tiaras, and the shawls.
Yahweh said to me, “Take a large tablet, and write on it with a man’s pen, ‘For Maher Shalal Hash Baz’;* “Maher Shalal Hash Baz” means “quick to the plunder, swift to the prey”.
